state: What a truly unique place. In another city, you would see this place and say, “They’re trying too hard to be different/modern.” Here in Charlotte, I can say it’s truly special. They live up to their promises and offer excellent bakery products as well as coffee and tea. 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. I didn’t expect to find something so authentic during a short visit, but this is exactly what I found. Don’t miss this opportunity if you come to Charlotte.

state: Here are the negatives: Bouchon Bakery is expensive and doesn’t offer seating. The positives are basically everything else. In terms of atmosphere, it’s a small kiosk filled with a variety of delicious desserts presented beautifully. A friendly and efficient staff handles a good number of customers. You can order hot drinks as well as desserts. I tried a spice-infused hot chocolate—it was a bit weak and not exactly irresistible, but still tasty. The desserts were amazing. I bought a croissant, a cheese danette, and a TKO. The croissant was crispy, with endless layers and rich butter flavor. It was one of the best croissants I’ve ever tasted. The cheese danette was undoubtedly the best cheese danette I’ve ever had—golden and delicious, perfect in every way, with a delightful cheese filling and lemon accents. The TKO followed the humble roots of Oreo, enhancing chocolate and white chocolate to a heavenly level, with a moist and crisp surface and creamy filling. I also bought some boxes of macarons—one as a gift and another to eat quickly. The box contained six flavors: raspberry, lemon, vanilla, espresso, chocolate, and pistachio. I was a little disappointed because there was no salty caramel, but it’s hard to be upset with good macarons. The macarons from Bouchon weren’t the best I’ve ever tasted, but they were very good, with soft shells and a light interior that delivered sugar without being overwhelming. I understand there are plans to open a Bouchon Bakery in Los Angeles. I really hope it won’t be nearby, as I think I wouldn’t be able to keep up with the sugar content of these desserts within a five-mile radius.

state: I wasn’t very impressed. We ordered a slice of nut cake, a chocolate-covered cheesecake, a biscuit and cream cupcake, and a colorful glaze cake slice. The nut cake was the only item with a decent taste. The chocolate-covered cheesecake was mediocre. The biscuit and cream cupcake was just a chocolate cupcake that was slightly dry and tasteless; the granulated glaze on top didn’t even resemble biscuits or cream at all. Don’t be fooled by the name “Carlos” and the photo of “Buddy” everywhere. You can get a better cake from a box in the store for $2 and save $20. The only reason this isn’t a star rating is because the staff were great.

state: After reading other reviews (and my sister’s personal experience), I was worried that the line would be very long. But on a Friday night around 8:45 PM, it took us only about 15 minutes. We ordered many desserts: chocolate éclair ($3.49), cream tartlet ($2.09), 4-inch red fruit tartlet ($4.89), lemon and cranberry tartlet ($4.89), small chocolate ganache pastelito (?), salty caramel brownies ($2.29), coconut cookies ($1.59), pistachio petit-four ($2.09), mini espresso mousse cups ($1.59), and all the French macarons in available flavors ($2.29). There were many staff members replenishing items, but only one person handling orders and one working at the checkout. Is this to control the line flow? It should slow down the line, as the person taking orders has to tell the cashier everything on the order. If the cashier doesn’t hear everything, it becomes chaotic. Personally, I didn’t try all the items we ordered, so I can only give my opinion based on my preference for sweets regarding some of the products… but the chocolate ganache pastelito is highly recommended. It isn’t too sweet, and I loved the filling. It can be shared between two people. The mini espresso mousse cup wasn’t as good as it seems. It’s small in size and not as fluffy as I wanted. The salty caramel brownies, if they aren’t the best (as seen in many other reviews), are one of the most popular items… but I thought the caramel was too much. Of course, it’s just the salt, and the brownie would be just regular chocolate brownies without it… because the brownie itself didn’t have a chocolate flavor that stood out. Finally, the cream tartlet is filled with cream pie filling, which I love, but it’s not worth $2. I mean, it’s large, so if you really like cream tartlets, go ahead. Order it alone or share it with someone else and ask for another item.

state:
Pros: It has the taste of ice cream.  
Cons: The cream melts very quickly, service is slow, and the staff are incompetent.  
My suggestion: It’s worth trying, but in the future I might choose DQ instead.  

We visited Jarling’s for the first time last night, after reading all the great reviews. It didn’t meet our expectations. When we arrived, there was already a long line at the door, so there were about 6 or 7 people behind our window. Even with 2 staff members working at that window, it took about 25 minutes to get ahead.  

When we finally got our chance, we ordered two bowls of ice cream for the kids, a waffle cone with ice cream for my fiancé, and a “blizzard” of chocolate with peanut butter paste (the equivalent of DQ’s “blizzard”) for myself. The employee who took our order clearly had no idea what he was doing. After wandering around for several minutes, he finally passed our order to another person. Still, it took a long time for our order to be prepared.  

Meanwhile, the man who seemed to be the manager just stood there, watching and shouting at customers in line to tell them to enter or leave, but not to close the door. When our order finally reached our window, it had melted. Then, the girl couldn’t operate the cash register, so it took a long time for me to get my change. By the time I got my order and walked to the picnic tables outside, melted cream was everywhere. The ice cream (or cream) was good, but not excellent, and definitely not worth the price. The “blizzard” was tasty and had a rich flavor of peanut butter. On the other hand, I ended up drinking almost everything. I wasn’t impressed.

state: Sprinkles was, to a large extent, what sparked the craze for cupcakes. It was time to get one here in Las Vegas. I’ve visited some of the locations in California, so I knew what to expect. However, if this is your first time visiting Sprinkles, I recommend keeping your expectations in check. Cupcakes aren’t cheap—about $4 per cupcake, and it gets even cheaper if you buy a dozen. Although it might seem expensive, the cupcakes here are definitely much better than those you can find at local supermarkets. When I visited this location, there was a long line both for the cupcakes and for the ice cream. Even though there were about 20 people in front of us, the line moved pretty quickly; it took around 20 minutes before we could enter. They offer a rotating menu each day, but of course, they also have some classic options available every day. The “dispenser box” next to the cupcakes helps save time if you know what you want. The most popular cupcake is the “red velvet” one, but I think the frosting is a little too sweet for my taste. Avoid the hard caramel on top, as it’s just for decoration. The wooden utensils are a nice touch, and the staff are excellent. Be adventurous and try some different flavors to see which one you like best!

state: During the 48 hours I spent in Cleveland, I visited Mitchell’s twice… which, I think, speaks volumes. The ice cream is amazing, and you can try different flavors without any restrictions. I tried the “Wildberry Crumble,” and it was delicious. What’s really great is that you can see how the ice cream is made in the “factory.” The store is located in an old theater, which adds to its charm. Even as a visitor, I could notice that Mitchell’s is a favorite place for both locals and tourists; it was always full. Fun fact: The “C” in Ohio has competing ice cream shops: Cleveland-Mitchell’s, Cincinnati-Graeter’s, Columbus-Jeni’s.

state: I was very excited to try this place, but it wasn’t as good as I expected. Seeing the long line, I thought the food would be excellent, but once I entered, the bakery products seemed quite mediocre. I knew from their appearance that the desserts wouldn’t be as good as they claimed, but I really wanted to try them, thinking there must be something really good here, considering everyone was eagerly waiting for delicious food. I ordered the most popular item in the store, and trust me, it definitely didn’t live up to expectations. I ordered two servings of lobster, a strawberry cake, and a chocolate-and-almond cupcake. After spending $27, I was quite dissatisfied. The only positive thing was the very kind cashier.

state: I have been searching relentlessly for your cookies, brownies, and “s’mores” cakes for a long time. But finally, I managed to get some. They aren’t exactly what I expected, but they’re still something. So, I bought the “s’mores” cake and a “Tres Leche” cake. My friend loves the “Tres Leche” cake, and I like the “s’mores” cake too. It’s very moist and delicious. I can’t say the customer service was perfect. The responses were very quick, both the first time and the second time. So, I didn’t try to insist or act too casual. It was my first time. It was quite crowded. The second time, it was the first Wednesday after opening, and it seemed like there was a private event going on at the same time. So, I felt a little pressured. Overall, I would love to come back and buy more “s’mores” cookies and cakes.

state: If you love creamy ice cream, this is the perfect place. There’s history and tradition, the beauty of the neon lights, and, of course, delicious ice creams. The place only accepts cash, so keep that in mind. It’s definitely a trip worth making. There’s a small parking lot, so you can sit down and enjoy your ice cream, as you’ll probably need to focus all your attention on it. Either because of nostalgia or because of the great ice cream, you’ll have fun!

state: Two words: Toffee Banoffi. We bought one and wanted four. Incredibly delicious. Alton Brown is right when he says this is one of “the best flavors I’ve ever tasted”. Ice cream with pieces of toffee, peanuts, caramel, banana, chantilly, and a bowl of crunchy waffles… how could anyone go wrong? The other flavors of ice cream were also delicious, but they were overshadowed by the sundae. Our waiter was very patient with our excessive tasting and spent time turning our sundae into a masterpiece. Sweet Republic is on par with other well-known ice cream shops I’ve visited: Bi-Rite, Ici, Salt & Straw, Creole Creamery, etc. I’ll come back if I’m ever in the area!

state: Yum. Even though I have one in my backyard in Newport, I still have to stop here when I'm at the LINQ Promenade. The best thing about this place is it has the cupcake ATM ! Its always busy but believe the hype. The cupcakes are all made with high quality ingredients that you can taste and the ice cream is just so creamy and their specialty flavors are my fave. I got the Lemon meringue ice cream and a cupcake with it on the side (I can never eat them together) HEAVEN. I also got a cookie cupcake to go and ate it this morning with my coffee. Out of the park good. My kid got the red velvet waffle cone with Cap'n Crunch ice cream. SOOO good. Service was nice, and helpful OH and don't forget to sign up for the rewards program!

state: I met a friend here to catch up and try their vegan donuts. The place is located on 6th Street in Carson, and there’s plenty of parking… just bring coins or a credit card. All spaces are paid for. I entered and was greeted by a very friendly team. Everyone was very kind and welcoming. My friend was already there, waiting with a green matcha vegan donut, a crème brûlée, and an apple donut. We went to the patio and started eating. The apple donut was the best I’ve ever had—crispy on the outside and soft and warm inside. There were real apple pieces scattered all over the donut. The green matcha donut was a delicious cake-style donut that wasn’t too sweet, with orange peel bits. It was really good. The crème brûlée was soft, with a delicious, thick cream. I was truly impressed… actually, when we finished, it was happy hour, so I bought a whole box for $5 and gave it to my family and friends. Definitely, this is my new favorite place to buy donuts. I can’t wait to come back and try more vegan options!

state: It was really fun ordering those donuts, haha! I went there to order special donuts for my boyfriend’s birthday, and ended up ordering them for the whole office! First, I had to take photos of all the available options, and then wait for their responses. The staff were very friendly and patient with me. Now, about the donuts… They were good! They weren’t as good as the “Donut Man” donuts from Los Angeles, but they were still delicious. My favorite was the Caramel Latte donut—it was sweet and creamy! The Strawberry Split was a bit dry. The Chocolate Euphoria was just okay. The Creme Brulee was really good, but it needed more cream in the middle. I think my favorite among them was the Old Fashion donut. I regret not ordering that last Nutella donut—I think I would have loved it! I’ll come back, but I really miss the quality donuts from “Donut Man” here in Las Vegas.

state: One word: Delicious. Two words: Great atmosphere. My opinion: Delicious in my stomach! Everyone should visit Amelie’s Bakery, located in NoDa. It’s much more than just a bakery; once you try it, you’ll understand why I say that. It’s almost like being in the home of a great (but eclectic) aunt who loves making cakes, croissants, breakfast sandwiches, and more to tempt your taste buds. I mention this place because you can consider it an experience—visit it whenever you want to enjoy a nearly epic moment with a partner, or to buy something for everyday use or a special occasion. Right now, surely you’re craving something delicious. Just remember that these delicious products can be obtained at any time, as it’s open 24 hours a day (what a blessing!).

state: 85C is a mandatory stop at Shanghai Plaza. My family, friends and colleagues love the pastries. We would have a box of 85°C at my work's break room and conference room at least twice a month lol. Selection: Assorted pastries are freshly baked and more affordable than other bakeries. It seems like there are always new goodies every time we visit. The beverage menu was just decent, we enjoyed the iced coffee and sea salt jasmine iced tea. We really just come here for the pastries lol Service: Staff is friendly, also hardworking! They would come in and out to restock the pastries as some of the goodies get sold within minutes of after the previous restock lol! Parking: FREE. Shanghai Plaza parking lot just outside the bakery. We prefer parking in the back at W Pioneer Ave. & Arville St. then just stroll around the plaza since it gets really packed in the front. Highly recommend!

state: If you're looking for soft ice cream in Pittsburgh, this is the perfect place. In addition to usual flavors like vanilla and chocolate—which are available at most places—Page’s offers a wide range of other flavors, such as orange, mint chocolate, amaretto, pumpkin, and many more. You really can’t go wrong with any of these soft ice cream flavors. It seems that these flavors change depending on the season; for example, pumpkin is only available on menu in autumn. Usually, I prefer a small, simple cone, but they have a great variety of ice creams and other ways to enjoy all the soft ice cream flavors. They also serve some savory dishes, which I haven’t tried yet. The lines can be long, but don’t let that stop you—the wait is worth it. Oh, and they only accept cash, but there’s a ATM next to the building.

state: I have eaten here three times and they never disappoint. Staff are friendly and make an effort to talk and get your order correct. Ghirardelli chocolate is my favorite, so I am some biased, but the ice cream, chocolate chip cookies and candy selection are out of this world. The first time I go, was sundae with Ghirardelli fudge and two kinds of ice cream. Of course I also bought a bag of assorted Ghirardelli squares to go. The second time I tried the large chocolate chip cookie. It was warm and filled with huge chocolate chips, tasting as freshly baked. Third time was waffle bowl sundae, with hot fudge and of course waffle bowl is fudge dipped as well. Had to have another one of those cookies too. This sundae was so big I nearly didn't finish all, but was worth every bite. My favorite part is how they give a free promotional flavor chocolate square at the door. Definitely recommend anyone in the area try this place for ice cream, cookies or brownies. And of course, chocolate!

state: My friends and my husband brought me here today. They had been here before. My friends said we were going for almond croissants, baked twice. And it was incredible. Yes, of course I had to try it… and it was the last one. I can’t even begin to describe the perfection I found in this dessert. (My husband had brought French macarons from here before. They were delicious.) But, oh! The almond croissants… I’ll have dreams about those almond croissants. And that’s not all. Rebecca was amazing; she helped me find the perfect drink. I said, “Something with caffeine, hot, sweet but not too much.” She replied without hesitation, “Mocha coffee with salty caramel.” Okay, that sounds great. No, “great” isn’t even a word that can describe how perfect that drink was. Creamy, smooth, perfect. In the car, on the way home (we live an hour away from here), I said to my husband, “Any day you want to come here, just tell me.” Thank you. Thank you for existing.

state: I was visiting Charlotte for my best friend's birthday weekend. We stopped in twice this weekend and I really enjoyed this bakery. The staff was nice and very helpful and patient explaining what the items were. I ended up buying a raspberry fruit tart, pistachio macarons, and their seasonal passion fruit strawberry lemonade to drink. All were really good! The tart was sweet, but not too sugary. Just enough tartness to it! I just recently started enjoying macarons and this was so fresh. The passion fruit strawberry lemonade had stronger hints of passion fruit and sparkling fruit soda, the strawberry lemonade taste was not as strong on my order. It was really great!!! I hope I can come back before I leave tomorrow night. I hope to find something similar to this bakery back home in the Philadelphia area.

state: I took the player to the airport and thought it would be good to eat something before heading home. This place was almost on the way… There isn’t much space between the doors and the pastry display, which is an excellent arrangement—very convenient for getting an orange macaron while deciding what to eat! According to legend, this is the original place, the home of the Provençal trailer style that everyone knows and loves. A “croque monsieur” half-eaten, accompanied by tomato soup with fennel and cold water—it seemed perfect. Usually, I’m not a big fan of red soups, but this one has fennel… and that made everything work out well, thank you very much! A delicious red soup, with texture and substance—not like those childhood soups! My sandwich was excellent: a generous layer of spicy Dijon mustard complemented the subtlety of grilled ham in thin slices, all inside a toasted croissant that was crunchy and covered in butter. Cheers to a great ham sandwich!

state:
Base for my star ratings (which mainly focus on food or drinks):

1 star: Never again.
2 stars: Bad food and experience; the measurements were extraordinary to make me want to return.
3 stars: Average, nothing really special, not particularly bad.
4 stars: Very good, definitely would return.
5 stars: A favorite, one of the best. Just an update after a long time. Still one of the best places to eat ice cream in the country. It still offers original and interesting flavor combinations, without exaggeration or excessive experimentation like other places. No tricks, just high-quality ice cream. This time, I tried the peach and cream flavor. The beauty lies in simplicity. Sweet cream ice cream with peach pieces. The sweet cream had the taste of milk I ate in France. Rich, sweet, and really looked like milk. It was creamy, indulgent, even. The peach pieces were a bit small, but they still added flavor and a slight sour contrast to the sweet cream.

state: Amelie’s offerings were acceptable, but in my opinion, the price and the wait in line weren’t worth it. I went with my girlfriend, her mother, and my mother, and we were able to try several different desserts. The salty caramel brownie was good. I really liked the brownie; the caramel coating was also acceptable, though not exactly what I expected. However, for $2.50, I would expect something more than just a small 1-ounce brownie. The eclairs were also fine. I didn’t really like the part of the dessert, but the vanilla and chocolate creams were quite tasty. My girlfriend and her mother were disappointed that the filling was cream instead of mascarpone, but they still enjoyed them. I tried a piece of chocolate cake too—it was pretty good, but it wasn’t worth $5 for a piece the size of a cupcake. After waiting 10 minutes in line (it was a Saturday night, and that’s quite long), and seeing how expensive the portions were, I assumed these desserts must be amazing. But everyone in my group agreed that they were just acceptable, nothing more.

state: This is my favorite bakery of all time (and I’ve tried many!). The large number of people at all times proves how amazing this place is! When I first entered, I was impressed, and my saliva glands started working as soon as I saw the long display of sweets. Everything was beautiful, and obviously, it was made with artistry by people who know what they’re doing. If you can’t find a sweet here that fully satisfies your visual and taste senses, maybe there’s something wrong with you. Plus, the diverse atmosphere is very welcoming, and it definitely makes you feel like you’ve traveled to Paris. But don’t be fooled—it’s not just the sweets that make people return to Amelie’s; the food itself is also delicious! I tried the ham and cheese cake and the sweet potato soup. The cake had just the right amount of high-quality cheese, and the bread underneath was crispy and tasty. It was also a perfect portion and not too expensive. The soup was very creamy and had the perfect balance of flavors. I love sweet potatoes, and I think they got the version of this soup just right. It’s perfect for a cold day! I tried the vanilla éclair and a mini fruit cake. The cake was the right size, and there were so many varieties that they all seemed perfect and fresh. The crust wasn’t too sweet, but it was perfect to complement the cream filling and the fresh fruits on top. The chocolate éclair was very big and didn’t have the shape of others I’ve tried before. However, the cream was delicious and there was plenty of it! You can also order a custom éclair for Valentine’s Day, which I can arrange next year. I heard that the salty caramel brownies are incredible, and I will definitely make the trip soon to try them and some other sweets! I hope to become a fan of Amelie’s!

state: The macarons were quite standard in quality, but expensive—unless you buy a package of 5 units. I would give them 4 stars, but the first time we tried to go there, it was a nightmare. We asked two employees at Venice where it was located; one gave us directions for “the nearest one” and said there were three locations, while the other said there was only one, and pointed out the one under the stairs, near Grand Lux. We arrived at that location 7 minutes before 9 o’clock (the closing time), and the place was empty. Thankfully, we got to the one facing the Strip about 3 minutes later, but it was also closed. That location opened up again the next morning when we returned, and I really wouldn’t have wanted to go at all, except that I really wanted the macarons before my return flight. On the other hand, there wasn’t any queue, and I really liked the packaging of the 5-unit package for travel.

state: Around Thanksgiving in 2019, I called to order a carrot cake, and this place came up in my mind. I didn’t ask directly but assumed they had carrot cakes available that day. When I arrived, they told me it was a weekend-only item, but could be ordered on weekdays if reserved in advance. One of the staff members helped me and made one for me. They said I could come back later. I was very happy. The carrot cake was well-received by the person who was going to receive it, and everyone loved it. There’s a layer of white chocolate in the middle of the cake, which gives it a crispy texture. It was incredible in terms of texture and flavor! I think the lobster pie was a bit dry, but that didn’t stop me from buying more in the future. A few days later, we went for coffee and dessert. All the desserts were of the same quality as the carrot cake. Everyone agreed that the coffee wasn’t exactly the best. I will continue to visit for their desserts, but probably I’ll buy my coffee elsewhere. There’s parking on the street.

state: Value: ***** Macarrones: ***** Service: (We were so enjoying it that we didn’t even worry about anything.) ***** I visited Bouchon Bakery for the first time 7 years ago during a trip to Manhattan, and I fell in love with their macarrones. Every visit to Manhattan requires a stop at Bouchon. I was excited to see that they have a location in Las Vegas, so when we planned a trip to Las Vegas, we made sure to stay near Bouchon. We loved being there at the Venetian, where we stayed! I’ve visited many other bakeries and tried many types of macarrones, but in my opinion, none are as good as those from Bouchon Bakery. Of course, this may be just a matter of opinion, since I’m not a chef, but the flavors of vanilla, caramel, and almond (my favorites) are exceptional, yet not too sweet. The cookie is soft and chewy, with a slight hard layer. But it’s the taste of the macarrones that impresses me—and theirs are twice as big as those from other bakeries. At $3.50 each, I think it’s an excellent value for money. We stopped every day of our trip to buy macarrones. I hope to visit other locations like Yountville someday. Macarrones and wine! For those who love sweetness, this is a must-visit place that you really should try.

state: I’m visiting Phoenix to watch the Dodgers’ preseason game with my daughter. We decided to stop for ice cream on the way back to the hotel. She searched on Yelp and found Novel, and we were very lucky to find it. First of all, it’s a really nice store with a large covered patio filled with tables and chairs. It’s bigger than it looks. Secondly, there are many unique flavors to choose from, and the owners encouraged us to try them all. I knew what I wanted after the second bite: “Tangerine Dream”. My daughter chose “Panna Cherry”. Both were delicious. Thirdly, the owners were very friendly, and we chatted with them while waiting for our ice cream. It surprised us that they had been open for just 10 days. They’re celebrating their grand opening in two days, and they were very happy with the results of their “pre-opening” period. They have everything needed to succeed. We wish them all the best.

state: Very much craft ice cream with some very unique flavors. I enjoyed it, but there is a lot going on, maybe too much in the flavors. Biggest pros were the fresh waffle cones (although they were very buttery) and the very friendly employees who had a well prepared statement about each flavor and made them all sound delicious. Biggest cons were, well the ice cream itself. Some of the flavors kind of gave me a food truck "we are trying really hard to be extremely unique" kind of vibe. Bangkok peanut ice cream is actually very spicy with a strong cayenne flavor. The sweet corn with blackberry tasted exactly how it sounds. I am definitely a fan of the brown butter almond brittle but a whole scoop of it is just too much. All in all, I would go back but I wouldn't seek it out or go out of my way, I certainly wouldn't wait in a line for 30 minutes again.

state: If you love crème brûlée, go to Sprinkles before July 31st to try their seasonal ice cream. This is the second time I’ve tried Sprinkles’ ice cream. I decided to try one of their cupcakes, along with an ice cream. I wanted to try their Cap n Crunch ice cream, but I found out that their seasonal flavor is crème brûlée. I couldn’t resist. I ordered an ice cream with a cupcake—you choose a cupcake and it’s cut in half, with a ball of ice cream placed between the two halves. Delicious! I also tried the vanilla cake with chocolate icing and sparkles. My boyfriend ordered Cap n Crunch ice cream and coffee in a red waffle cone. Everything was very delicious. The prices weren’t too high, considering they’re in a tourist area. Usually, you have to wait a little, so keep that in mind. If you don’t want to wait, you can always go to the side area and use their cupcake machine. It’s a fun experience. It’s a small and cozy place. The staff are friendly, and you can try different flavors of ice cream. Everything is quite sweet, but in a pleasant way. Maybe you’d like to order a drink to pair with the cupcakes, as they have plenty of icing.

state:
UPDATE: I visited the Milk Bar again and had a better experience. It still seems a bit expensive, but this time I tried the “crack pie” ice cream with crunchy corn, and it was really delicious!! I also tried the milk ice cream with cereal. It was definitely different from what I had before. The taste was much better!

I was really excited to try it. I watched an episode of “Chef’s Table” about this place and thought it looked really good. Unfortunately, it didn’t live up to expectations. The milk ice cream with cereal had too strong of a flavor—if that makes sense. I think it should be more subtle. That was the biggest disappointment. I didn’t like it very much. However, I really liked the “crack pie” and we’ll go back another day to try something else. I’m disappointed by the high prices. $6 for a small ice cream? $6.50 for a slice of “crack pie”? I make cakes at home and know that these ingredients aren’t expensive or difficult to prepare. The prices need to be reduced.

state: Got CRACK? I stopped by Milk Bar this evening before dinner because I enjoy my "dessert FIRST"... Awkward?! I dig the bakeries store front it's pretty hip and kind of reminds me of a food truck vibe. I ordered (2) corn cookies and (2) quakes CRACK PIE & BIRTHDAY CAKE for a total about $29 bucks. The corn cookies were amazing and full of flavor. I enjoyed the buttery cornbread tamale-like taste!Worth $3 bucks and definitely a must order. The Crack Pie Quake was sweet and delicious! Highly recommended if your a sweets junkie like myself. I was extremely disappointed in the Birthday cake quake. It was bland/flavorless I'm curious if an ingredient was skipped!! Considering the fresh products and local dairy used the pricing is decent. Regrettably, most people are use to Jack N The Box pricing which is pretty harsh to compare to an award winning pastry chefs recipes. My one gripe is it took exactly 15 minutes to prepare my two quakes with three employees on staff (I was the only person in line by the way). Two of the girls appeared very unsure of the ingredients. I witnessed a few people walking away because of the obnoxiously long wait without even being acknowledged. I'm likely to return I have a few more cookies with my name on them!!!

state: Modern but feels old fashion. I ordered the rocky road sundae. How rocky was this road? Well if I were driving Grandma around, her dentures would be rattling and once we get to the destination, she may have lost them somewhere between here and there. So if you can't picture it, the rocky road is loaded with almonds. I loved the almonds and was the best part of the sundae. The chocolate ice cream was creamy but too sweet for me. The flambÃ© marshmallow fluff was beautiful and enticing, but too sweet for me. I ordered a pretzel cone on the side to try as I read good reviews... it was kind of ehh. I would absolutely come back to try more of their imaginative menu. I was surprised at the sticker price on the menu, so be prepared. I came late at night so parking wasn't an issue, but it may be an issue during prime time. Oh those nuts... Grandma, can we go on another ride?

state: Ugh! This was so disappointing! For someone to be the boss of all cakes, you'd think the cake would blow your mind, or at the absolute least, be some of the better cake you've ever tasted. Unfortunately that is not the case. My sister and I both got to-go items from here after a late night dinner at Buddy V's at the Venetian. We took them back to our hotel. I opted for the funfetti cake. It ended up being too late to eat mine and I don't like cold cake anyways (they refrigerate their cake which I get why they do it, but I prefer it be room temperature when I dine on it). I ended up eating it the next night and I took the first bite and must have made a face because my sister said "what's wrong?" and I said "Hmmm nothing... this just tastes like boxed cake. It's not really that good at all." I mean really, I can name NUMEROUS bakeries in Columbus, Oh (including our grocery store bakery, Giant Eagle) that are better than this place. I would say the cake part tasted like boxed funfetti cake and the frosting tasted cheaper than canned icing. So all in all, I think I'd actually prefer Pillsbury and would label it a tad better than this cake. I can't say for sure if the cake in their Hoboken location would be better, but I think it's safe to assume they'd use all the same ingredients because it's the same ownership. After this visit, I am wondering if the Cake Boss only became famous for his presentation of cakes, and not the actual taste. Anyways, main positive about this place is the line management. We were there so late on a Sunday that there wasn't much of a line, but there is someone waiting right there with an Ipad helping you out as soon as you walk in. Friendly, helpful staff. Anyways, I'd recommend passing on this. Take a walk down to The Linq and opt for a Sprinkles cupcake instead...

state: January 2017 update: This place still impresses me. The food is always good, and the only thing I can say is that sometimes they run out of items. When I asked about this, they told me that they only buy products from certain suppliers (specifically, they only buy beef ribs from another shop). This seems to indicate good quality control. And their hygiene is excellent: recently, I saw a customer (who seemed to be a worker at West Side Market, which makes the situation even more frustrating) throw her order back into the pan because she was upset that she didn’t get a discount. They discarded the item and then cleaned and heated up the pan again, although it took a few extra minutes during a busy day. Great work! For those who complain about long lines and poor service, this is a great spot in a crowded market! If you don’t want to wait in line, just avoid it. It’s clear that this stand is designed to function, not to replace the experience of a restaurant with attentive servers. Previous review from August 2015: The crepes are always amazing, though the line can be quite long during peak times. Just calm down and wait for your food to arrive!

state: I was very excited to try this, but the excitement quickly faded. I bought a portion of nut cake for about $6–7. If that’s a “portion,” I would really like to see their version of a small portion, because that’s exactly what it was! At that price, they should offer a generous portion. It was okay, just a cold nut cake without the nuts. I asked them to prepare it “in the style,” but they said it wasn’t possible. So I bought a small chocolate ice cream with pretzels and cereal milk for another $6–7. The consistency was good, but there was hardly any flavor. I noticed salt in the chocolate, but actually, there wasn’t any chocolate at all. Therefore, I give them an A for their marketing strategy and a C- for their product. A good marketing strategy can make anything seem good—just be careful! :)

state: Sloan’s is definitely a place that reminds me of Florida. Three of my school hangouts—Clematis Street, City Place, and Mizner Park—have this ice cream shop: Sloan’s. This location, inside Venetian’s Grand Canal Shoppes, offers many of the same desserts, but you won’t find the distinctive transparent restrooms of Sloan’s. There’s a flavor for every craving—from coffee and donuts to apple pie. For about $10, I ordered a sundae with three balls, chantilly, hot chocolate sauce, and a topping. The hot chocolate sauce was lacking in quality. “Luv It” in Las Vegas makes this sundae much better. A “Kitchen Sink” brownie that looked good behind the glass might have been frozen beforehand. It would be much better if it were fresh, straight from the oven, when the toppings are melted and sticky, rather than hard. They also offer big donuts from the Donut Bar, caramelized apples, chocolate sauce, and more. But I come here just for the ice cream and to feel a little bit of Florida.

state: This place was excellent! The homemade, artisanal ice cream was, without a doubt, one of my favorite ice creams so far. If you’re traveling through Phoenix, like us, this is a place you absolutely cannot miss. We enjoyed the honey and lavender ice cream, as well as the bourbon and pecan ice cream. The honey and lavender ice cream is calm, but also sweet. The lavender has a hint of honey, making it like walking through a field of lavender under the sun. The bourbon and pecan ice cream was sweet and very creamy. The owner was very kind and treated us as if we were part of his “ice cream club”. We really enjoyed chatting with him while tasting the ice creams. As my teenage children said, “Some of the best ice creams I’ve ever tasted. I’m glad I don’t live here, otherwise I would be broke from coming here every day!” The price is very reasonable. It’s exactly what I would expect to pay for a portion. The location of the ice cream shop is cozy—a lovely patio where you can enjoy ice cream and share the joy of ice cream with friends and family. Thank you for creating such a wonderful ice cream shop! We would love for them to open another one here in Greensboro, North Carolina! We hope to visit again and enjoy the ice cream once more.

state: Exterior = 4/5 This place is located next to Momofuku on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan. It is almost like a stand so there is no seating area for it specifically - though there is seating near by or you could grab a slot machine (play and eat). The line was small when we got there so no major wait. It was nicely decorated, and definitely eye catching with the neon "Milk" sign. Interior = 3/5 Not much of an interior, since it is a stand alone stall almost. They have a cart in front of the cashier where you can get napkins and the utensils. Along the cashier, they have their cookies. Their menu is located on the wall directly behind the cashier. Service = 5/5 The ladies working the cashier and the food items were quick to move and get the items as you ordered. So there was basically no lag time between ordering and receiving your items. Their quickness almost had me struggling to pay and hold my items. Order = 3/5 Crack pie: 3/5 We felt this was a little hyped up, and it didn't really specify a flavor type. It was a kind of tiny triangle of pie, not very thick either. When I bit into it, it reminded me of butterscotch. It was also pretty chewy. Cereal Milk with cornflakes: 3/5 The ice cream didn't really have a flavor that I found I could nail down. The cornflakes itself seemed like they were sweetened, but not in the way Frosted Flakes are. I felt they were more crunchy than your usual corn flakes. I was thrown off as the combination seemed almost salty somehow. Fruity Milk with cornflakes: 3/5 Light fruity flavor. Boyfriend found there to be a slight chalky after taste. The cornflakes, added a nice crunch, but also had an interesting flavor. For me, I preferred this over the Cereal Milk since it didn't seem to have a salty flavor (which I think is attributed to the cornflakes). Overall = 3/5 It was good to try, but I'm okay with not running back next time I am in Vegas. If you like cookies, they also have a selection of cookies to choose from that are pre-packaged. The price was a bit much for the quantity of the items and ice served. Did find the saltiness/after taste of the ice cream a bit weird. Hint = Grab a cookie for on the go munching. They have a deal if you buy three!

state: I have been waiting to try this place since moving to Charlotte. It's a good place for sweets and I'll for sure be back again. I would like to say that I'm someone who does not like overly sweet, sugary things. I grew up eating Japanese cake and sweets, if that gives you an idea. Said in bubble tea terms: I order my sugar 25%. 50% sugar is my max and this is only if I'm wanting that sugary taste. Cheesecake: First off, I was shocked that this place actually made baked cheesecake instead of the pour and cool in the fridge type. This is the type of cheesecake seen in Japan. However, the chocolate chips ruined it for me. You can't see it in the picture but the inside is PACKED with more chocolate chips. I felt like I took a handful of chocolate chips, shoved it in my mouth and then added a small bite of cheesecake. I tried hard to assess just the cheesecake portion but it was difficult. I *think* the cheesecake was ok? It was the right amount of sweetness and tartness. My husband who loves cheesecake and chocolate got this for himself and loved it. So I think I'm just the anomaly here. Red velvet cake: I'm a sucker for red velvet. The cake was SUPER moist. Just for that, I would get it again. The cake sponge was not overly sweet and I savored every bite. Downside: there was waaaaay too much icing surrounding the cake. I could not eat the "spine" of the cake with icing and tossed it out. But the amount of icing between the layers of cake was perfect. The icing is pretty sweet but it was balanced out by the cake. I just wish they didn't slather so much on the outside Cannoli: So this is made fresh at the counter and you can customize it however you want. Husband got the simplest-- sweet cream with chocolate chips. I think I'm just not a cannoli person. So I think it's unfair for me to judge this item. I will say, a lot of my friends LOVE their cannoli. And I have to admit, even though I thought it was meh, this was the first cannoli that was edible for me, which is saying a lot. So if you're a cannoli person, I would say, get it. Napoleon: Best for last. I can't even describe how amazing this was. It's a huge slice and I wanted another one. I can't stop thinking about this! The custard/cream was the perfect sweetness and the puffy layers were sooo good!! FYI, it gets a little messy to eat because the custard will leak out. But I love that they didn't skimp out on the custard. I will absolutely be craving and getting this again!!!! I honestly think I would have given this place a 3 star but this ONE dessert deserved a star of it's own. Overall, I thought this place was standard. I've definitely had better sweets from both Italian and French bakeries. But the Napoleon? Man, that was so good! I want to get several different items next time and reassess. With the Napoleon aside, this place got a 4 star because of their great and friendly customer service (some bakeries can be snobby and rush customers to pick their items), countless selections of baked goods, and the fact that they don't overly sweeten their items. Reading the other reviews here, hearing what my friends have said about this place, I understand that I probably do not have the palate of the majority. I can't in good faith give this place 3 stars because I am weird about sweets. But this definitely was not the best Italian bakery I have tried. Therefore, 4 stars.

state: The first time I went to Crêpes De Luxe, my intention was to write a negative review. Of course! The crepe I received back then was just as delicious as the one I got recently—with Nutella, strawberries, and bananas inside a fresh and warm crepe. But that attitude turned out to be a disaster. The staff seemed annoyed and cold, with an unpleasant expression on their faces, which would make me hesitate to go to their counter at West Side Market on a busy day! It was worse than “Soup Nazi”—at least there were set rules to follow. But in some ways, they were right. In fact, I asked for that kind of service. On my last visit, someone in their twenties took care of me on a Wednesday morning, and his attitude was much more pleasant. He even had enough patience to serve six elementary school girls during a field trip, with a smile. My best advice for those who go to Crêpes De Luxe is: try to avoid going when the market is crowded. The crepes will always be delicious, but the taste is even better with great service.

state: This place satisfied my sweet tooth with a lovely display of its spread of offerings. The oatmeal scotchie cookies were probably something I could have made at home but was nice to be able to pick them up ready to go- delicious, we got the butterscotch chip bars to go along with. Not often something I find in other bakeries so I was really happy! The hamburger buns were so soft and reminded me of my grandmas homemade buns- I could tell everything is made with high quality ingredients because the two buns we didn't eat had mold growing on them after a few days on my counter, unlike the preservative filled bread you find in a grocery store- sad for me that we didn't eat them fast enough! The cracked wheat loaf was very good also. I live on the west side but will make a special trip to Batch if I am in need of high quality bakery items.

state: A huge line to enter, lasting about half an hour. This made me think it must be a very good place. When we reached the front, they pressured us to make our choices quickly and asked if we could decide soon because of the long line. It wasn’t just a rude attitude; the famous bakery really wasn’t worth waiting for at all. We ordered cannoli with chocolate and Oreo cookies. We were all very disappointed and realized that we had wasted half an hour. There was no seating available, the staff was rude—both when handling the line and when taking orders and processing payments at the counter. I won’t go there again.

state: I called the bakery on Friday morning to order a cannoli cake. I was told that the cake would cost $65 and would be ready by 12:30 p.m. on Sunday. When I arrived at the bakery, it was indeed ready, and it looked amazing!! I was very satisfied with the cake, but I was charged an extra $5.00 compared to the price mentioned over the phone. So, I decided to buy some cookies for my mother’s birthday. Since my boyfriend is from New York, I wanted to try the colorful cookies before buying them, as they were his mother’s favorite. The cashier asked the attendant if he could get a cookie, and he replied, “Well, you’ll have to buy it yourself.” We had planned to spend around $100 there, and couldn’t he just try the cookies? Seriously? The attendant charged us $1.00 per cookie. Maybe I would give it 5 stars if the customer service was better. I’ll update you on how the cake turns out later, but it seems really delicious.

state: First of all, 85* isn’t a bad bakery. Some of its products, like egg cakes and milk bread, are good. I also love black tea with sea salt cream, and my husband loves Thai tea. However, the service here is absolutely terrible. There’s a lack of staff, and employees are slow. I understand that 85* is popular, and Las Vegas has been waiting eagerly for its opening. It doesn’t surprise me that it’s always full, but every time I go there, there are always lines and no products available. The staff have to do multiple tasks instead of just serving customers. This makes the payment process inefficient, as it takes a long time. They not only have to count the products and enter them into the system, but they also have to assemble the transport boxes and put each item individually into plastic bags before organizing them into boxes. All this can take up to 5 minutes, even before they start collecting money. I’ve been to several 85* locations in California, and I know this is common regarding service, but with so many customers visiting, it doesn’t seem efficient. At least, they could prepare the transport boxes in advance or eliminate the individual packaging to speed things up. Additionally, the staff work very slowly. I understand they’re all new, but it’s important to have urgency when there’s a crowd. It’s frustrating to see staff taking time in lines across multiple corridors, especially when you’ve already waited over 30 minutes just to be served. Last time we went there, my husband ate a pastry while we waited because he was hungry, and the line took a long time. We also saw a man literally drop his tray full of pastries on a nearby counter and leave, because he didn’t want to wait any longer. I’m curious whether the staff threw away the pastries or put them back on the shelves for sale. Either way, it’s a loss for the business. Of course, I told the staff that my husband ate a pastry (the packaging was still on the tray), but I’m curious how many other customers ate their products while waiting without telling the staff. With so many people, it’s easy to go unnoticed. Also, while my husband waited in line, I went to the self-service kiosk to buy drinks, as it was faster at a separate counter. The screen showed Thai tea, which was “buy one, get one free” from December to early January. I ordered Thai tea, but didn’t see any message about a free drink, so I asked the staff. She seemed confused at first, then said, “Oh, we don’t have that promotion here, because we’re just starting.” I asked why it was advertised if it wasn’t offered. Her answer was, “We can’t remove it from the screen. Sorry.” I just ignored it. It’s not against the staff. She was polite and was just doing her job, but if something is advertised and it’s a franchise, at least let people know it’s not valid here or something similar. Otherwise, it’s just false advertising and unethical behavior. If it’s not a valid promotion, it should be removed, otherwise, it should still be offered if it’s advertised. Anyway, I’m not complaining about free Thai tea, but I found it strange. This really contributes to poor management, lack of staff, and lack of organization at this place. I hope they can fix this in the future. As I said, 85* isn’t a bad bakery.

state: I’ve been to New York before, but unfortunately, I didn’t have enough time to try the Milk Bar. I heard many good things about this place, so I was very excited to try it out. Fortunately, I got to taste their birthday cookies and ice cream while dining at Momofuku in January. Both were really delicious. So, I’m glad that the Milk Bar is open next to it, so I can satisfy my craving for sweets. I came here in January before my trip back to buy some cookies. The staff described all the cookies to me, and when they said the blueberry and cream cookies tasted like blueberry muffins, I was convinced. I bought a few of those, along with a cornflake cookie, a compound cookie, and a chocolate with marshmallow cookie. Definitely, I liked the blueberry cookies the most. They’re a bit expensive, but I think they’re worth it. I came back in April and bought more cookies. All were blueberry and chocolate. In my opinion, these two are the best. I also bought cereal ice cream with fruit pieces. The cereal with fruit pieces has a slight saltiness that balances the sweetness. It’s really pleasant. Finally, I bought ice cream here at 10 a.m. There’s never too early to satisfy your sweet tooth. Besides, you’re on vacation. Enjoy! haha The Milk Bar and its sweets are really great. So good that my friend who lives in Las Vegas brought some cookies for me when she visited. The staff is very friendly and knows the products well. During both visits, there were no lines, which is great. I’m addicted. The cookies (and ice cream) are divine. They’re so good that I can’t wait to try them again when I return to Las Vegas in September! Do yourself a favor and buy some of these—you won’t regret it.

state: Best soft-served ice cream I ever had. At first when receiving a very dauntingly large ice cream cone I was worried about my ability to finish it. But to my surprise tthe ice cream was perfect. The temperature was perfect wasn't too cold and didn't melt to fast. The matcha flavor of the ice cream was definitely present but not over powering with the addition of the vanilla swirl to add some extra flavor. The ice cream had the perfect amount of sweetness. I don't have a sweet tooth but I still able to finish the ice cream in one sitting. The ice cream was flavor were very subtle easily melting in your mouth yet somehow so perfect in making you addicted to taste more. If you're not trying this ice cream and you're from the area you are definitely missing out.

state:
My husband and I really love this place. Although we couldn’t sit inside (due to COVID, there were only options for bringing things with), the atmosphere was incredible, and we really wish we had been able to enjoy more. It felt like one of those entertainment halls from the time of “The Great Gatsby”. Red velvet sofas, antique furniture, warm yellow lighting, and beautiful fabrics everywhere! Butterwood had an amazing selection of desserts and cakes—you wouldn’t believe it—and also many vegan options. In the end, we chose:  
– Poppy Rose cake with fig cream  
– Carrot cake with spices and coffee-cinnamon buttercream  
– Orange blood cake with almond buttercream  
All of them were absolutely fantastic—we shared them with my cousin and her boyfriend. The Poppy Rose cake was our favorite; it was moist, delicious, and had those subtle poppy and pink flavors that matched perfectly. We also ordered two hot chocolates. Hot chocolates were quite common, so they weren’t worth it. Instead, try more of those chewable desserts! Five stars, despite the hot chocolates, because they were really good.

state: This giant brownie is incredible – it’s very tasty. Without a doubt, it’s the most delicious brownie I’ve ever tasted. It has a generous layer of fudge in the middle, a Graham cracker base at the bottom, and layers of baked marshmallows. I loved every bite of this giant brownie; it truly impresses. Additionally, the oat cream cakes are absolutely worth trying – they’re fantastic. Both items are the best-selling products at Batchmaker. As it was my first visit (and certainly not the last), I had to try both. Oh, and I can’t forget about the cookies – they might be the best in the city. The menu is extensive, and I can guarantee that the Oreo cookies with chocolate, caramel, and peanut butter are amazing. Batchmaker has become my favorite bakery in town. Since I’m a fan of cakes, I’m really excited to try the cakes there. You need to order in advance so I can share my experiences soon. I just hope the opening hours would be more convenient, but I understand that, like Cristina, the owner of Batchmaker, she runs everything by herself. I had to wait a while for the popularity to decrease, as the products ran out quickly. I will come back (voice of Arnold).

state: I was introduced to Mitchell’s a few years ago, and I have never been back since. Mitchell’s ice cream is a wonderful store. All the ice cream is made in-house, and this specific location of Mitchell’s has a small factory inside, which can be seen through the glass behind the counter. The store is huge. The lines are always full, which shows how popular this place is. I tried some items from Mitchell’s, but my favorite is the bitter chocolate ice cream with mint pieces. What I like is that there are big chunks of bitter chocolate in the ice cream, and it isn’t colored green. It has a great mint flavor, without being overdone. Usually, I like to order the ice cream as a sundae with hot chocolate sauce and extra whipped cream. I love their whipped cream, and I would buy an entire pot just to eat everything at once. I love ice cream, and Mitchell’s is the perfect place for those who enjoy ice cream.

state: I really loved the chocolate and mint ice cream! I had high expectations when coming here, thanks to the reviews on Yelp and the fact that it’s supposedly one of the best in the United States. Usually, when this happens, I find that the product isn’t as good as I expected, and I feel very disappointed. But this place is definitely an exception. The owner was very kind to our group. We wanted to take a small portion home, but we didn’t want the ice cream to melt during a one-hour trip. She prepared the portion in a brown bag with ice and stored it in the freezer while we enjoyed our portions there. My favorites were the chocolate and mint ones, and the strawberry one. You can tell the freshness of the ingredients. Next time, I’ll give myself the chance to try some of their other delicious treats.

state: I completely forgot how amazing Batch was, until my recent trip back to Madison. I’m glad they finally moved to the larger store, which, in my opinion, means they’ll have more interesting products to offer. And I wasn’t disappointed. I’ve bought many great items from Batch, from their wheat breads to the famous “monkey bread.” One of my favorite desserts since childhood is the “morning bun.” I felt like a child in a candy store when I saw that Batch had its own version. As Corey D would say, “What a Batch!” That big ball of buttery dough, covered with sticky caramel, could be one of the best “morning buns” I’ve ever eaten… believe me, I’ve eaten many. It might even compete with Simma’s in Milwaukee. That alone would warrant 10 stars, but unfortunately, Yelp only allows five! I need to try one of their salty options and a challah bread next time I’m in town!

state: This ice cream shop, located at the Memorial Union of the University of Wisconsin, serves ice cream from Babcock Hall, which seems to be very popular in the area. I’m not surprised: the ice cream is really good. My wife chose the chocolate ice cream with orange slices and sugar cubes—she praised it highly. My ice cream with cookie pieces was also good, but not as special as hers. My five-star rating depends not only on the quality of the ice cream, but also on the cost-effectiveness: our sugar cubes cost just $2.60 each, which is quite reasonable considering the generous amount we received. The place is also pleasant: you can take your sugar cubes outside and sit on the porch of M.U., where you can enjoy a stunning view of the lake. It’s worth a visit.

Definitely reasonable prices. I must say I really like cream brûlée donuts. They’re my favorites, and I also liked the Nutella donut. But undoubtedly, cream brûlée donuts are my favorite. state: I heard of this place before, but it’s known for its high standards and excellent reputation. Since not all of us could afford to go to the original location, we went to the bakery right across from the Opera’s Phantom Theatre. It was around breakfast time, so I bought a croissant and a carrot cake biscuit. The croissant was very soft and had a lot of buttery flavor. I also liked the carrot cake biscuit, but it’s quite sweet. I couldn’t eat everything at once, so I saved some for later. I thought about going back to buy some macarons—they’re the biggest ones I’ve ever seen—but I didn’t go back, so I’ll have to wait until next time. *Update*: Finally, I tried the vanilla and raspberry macarons. Delicious! Soft, with plenty of filling and lots of flavor. They’re bigger than the small macarons served in many other places, but they cost about the same as $3.

state: I think this review is going to be along the same lines as everyone else. I was hankering for some sweets late at night, ok it wasn't that late, maybe 8 or so, and I looked for some dessert spots. Turns out we weren't too far from AmÃ©lie's French Bakery. I hate parking so I looked them up on Google Maps before heading out and saw they had a parking lot right in front so I figured it wouldn't be too bad and I was right, we found a spot right away. The line was long. It did wrap around and through 2 rooms. It also moved fast. I timed it, because why not? It took 25 minutes from walking in to walking out. That's not bad at all. I got to hear a lovely (not) conversation behind me, so it was interesting to say the least. The space is super cute and cozy, though we got ours to go. I can see why people would like to come here and work or hang out with friends. We ordered a variety of desserts. Lemon & raspberry meringue; salted caramel & espresso torts; salted caramel brownie; 2 macaroons; 2 chocolate croissants for the following morning. The best thing was the Lemon & Raspberry meringue. The worst things were the macaroons. The torts were excellent and the salted caramel brownie was just okay. The croissants were pretty good though. I think I am biased though. My heritage is French and my mom is an excellent baker, so things first get judged by how my mom makes them and secondly by a place in my hometown that made a croquembouche for my wedding, who is directly from France. His macaroons are the best things I've ever had. I think my expectations were too high for a place that is always packed and is open 24hrs. I think their quality suffers because of the quantity they need to produce to keep up with demand. It did however meet the "late night desserts" urge that I had!

state: I paid $6.50 for a dessert cup, and also paid an extra $1 for a toasted marshmallow. Fatty Daddy offers flavors of ice cream and macarons that are quite common; nothing very original or exotic. As for the ice cream, they were almost without Nutella; not enough to make a full cup, but I still tried it and found it good. They didn’t have the caramel macaron, and I didn’t want vanilla or strawberry options either. I’m not a fan of coconut, and I know the “Fruity Pebbles” are popular, but I’ve never been a big fan myself. My only remaining option was red velvet. Salted caramel is usually one of my favorites, so I didn’t even think about trying it first. I thought it would go well with the red velvet macaron, so I chose that instead. Of course, I had to add a toasted marshmallow to give it a special touch. I liked the concept of the dessert cup, and I appreciate what they’re trying to do. However, it was too sweet for me… and I have a strong appetite for sweets. The salted caramel ice cream didn’t have a pleasant taste. It was a disappointment, especially considering the price. But if you’re doing this for social media, go ahead, but don’t expect a surprising experience. However, I must say that the person there was very friendly, and the other flavors we tried were quite enjoyable.

state: Presti’s best dessert is its fruit tart with cream – only available on weekends. The cannoli are acceptable, but if bought later, they tend to be soft and cold. Other desserts vary depending on their freshness. However, Presti still serves desserts that aren’t in their best condition, which is surprising. I visited this place frequently during this semester due to its excellent atmosphere. It’s my “happy place” in Cleveland. Although the lunch dishes look appealing when seen through the glass, they need some improvements. It’s not about major changes, but small details like adding salt or spices, preventing the pasta from steaming in its own sauce for hours, or providing enough filling in the strombolis. When they have sandwiches available, buy them! They’re probably the only delicious item on the lunch menu. My favorite dessert. The coffee is awful: tasteless, with small oily spots on the surface. The tea is acceptable, and they have a good variety. My younger brother loves hot chocolate with cream. In defense of Presti, despite some questionable foods, the service is excellent. I love the older woman with blond hair and a big smile. They’re always willing to help, and that’s enough to make me return again and again. I visit this place constantly, and I’ve only found one exception to this rule: a younger waiter with dark hair and a very bad attitude. Once I asked him to warm up my chicken pie, which was frozen, and he overcooked it, forgot about it, and then threw it at me when I asked him to return it without apology. I guess he had a bad day, or he’s just a bad person. I’ve avoided that waiter since then. To be honest, although I love Presti and return frequently, I don’t think it could survive if there were more competition. They need to rethink their lunch menu, or stop offering it altogether. And if the desserts are old, don’t sell them. It’s not worth damaging your reputation. The only viable competitor is Corbo’s, which is right next door, but it’s not enough to bring about significant change.

state: Well, obviously it’s a very famous place for its excellent cakes, sandwiches, soups, and drinks. This place is very special to me and my wife, and we have many wonderful memories here. The fact that it’s open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, adds an extra value to it. My favorites are the salty caramel brownies, chocolate cake, chicken sandwich, almond cake (delicious), and chai tea latte with soy milk. This was the first place where we tried the chai tea latte with soy milk, and that flavor has become a regular taste. undoubtedly, the atmosphere gives you a French feel, or at least you’ll learn to appreciate French flavors. On Fridays and Saturdays in the evening, it’s usually very busy, as many people come here to enjoy their favorite dishes after a party. Additionally, thanks to Wi-Fi, it’s an ideal place to work or study. If you like cakes, it’s a must-visit place in Charlotte.

state: As a future mother, hunger hits quickly, even when you least expect it. We were so busy exploring the attractions and sounds of the Strip that we lost track of time for dinner. Nausea and dizziness started before I even knew what to do. My husband, with his quick thinking, said, “Let’s get some cupcakes, since we can’t decide which restaurant to eat at, and we’ll still have to wait for food after ordering.” He knew me very well. I chose a dark chocolate cupcake with sprinkles (obviously), and it was amazing how quickly I felt better. Of course, cupcakes can do that, even if you’re not pregnant and feeling hungry.

state: Carlos bakery is my favorite bakery. I had been dying to go to this place for the longest time. The lines are always very long everytime I had gone. And the place is pretty dang hard to find in the Venetian! I had tried to figure out the best times to go, as sometimes I'd go on a Friday at noon and understandably they are packed. I mean packed. I mean a line like a ride at a theme park. Today however, ahhhh today was different. Today was MY day. Today was the day that I would get to eat baked goods from the great cake boss. I decided who would go on a Wednesday at 4pm? Boom. Only a short line. I looked for about 10 minutes and there was so many decisions. These are big decisions. Not life or death obviously. But big in my mind. So....I got the carrot cake and 2 red velvet cupcakes. It came to about $15 which is expensive but also fair. They put them in a nice little box so I could take it home and enjoy. I don't have much else to say about the place. It is well maintained, clean, and the people are friendly. You can see the workers in the window working on the food. Now how were the baked goods? Delicious! They were among my favorite for the red velvet cupcakes. And the carrot cake was superb as well. Like I . But like I said the lines can be crazy long and finding the place is quite a challenge. So my advice, go there, and if the line is tooooooo long then come back another time. Like say Wednesday around 4pm.

state: Oh my God! I’m hesitant to say “the best,” but this is undoubtedly the most delicious ice cream I’ve ever tasted. I ordered a chocolate cone with pecans and another waffle cone with bananas. I love waffle cones, but they’re also the safest option here—regular sugar cones aren’t big enough to hold the ice creams properly. Flavor: rich and made with genuine ingredients. The banana cone contained real banana pieces, with a true banana flavor. The chocolate cone with pecans had whole, salty pecans mixed into a creamy, medium-sweet chocolate. Sweetness: not overwhelming or excessive—the honey really provides just the right amount of sweetness. Texture: not too hard, nor too soft; doesn’t melt easily, refreshing and creamy with a slightly icy texture, without causing a heavy feeling in the head. Price: one order includes 2 generous cones for less than $4. Target audience: I went on a Sunday night; the lines were long, but service was relatively quick. This is a true treasure from a small business that no chain store could replicate. The quality is even better than my favorite ice creams from stores like Ben & Jerry’s and Movenpick. I just wish there was a way to send some back to my friends in Los Angeles! I’ll definitely return to try the special flavors each month—I can’t wait to try cinnamon, pumpkin, and coffee flavors in October!

state: Is there a better way to gain some extra weight after dinner at Windsor? The solution is to go to Churn, which is right next to there! I ate the traditional buttery ice cream with nuts. You can choose between the baked cookies on the counter and the flavor of the ice cream. Unfortunately, the ice cream wasn’t frozen, so it melted quickly on a hot summer day. I might wait until it’s a little cooler before trying other flavors in a pretzel cone.

state: When it comes to bakeries, Presti’s is one of the best, in my opinion. They have sweets, cookies, and an incredible variety of delicious products. It was a natural choice when I was invited by a very dear friend to bring sweets to a dinner event to honor her father, which happened nearby by chance. To make it clear, the tray with 25 small sweets and the tray with 1.3 kg of cookies I ordered were wonderful, and they were greatly appreciated by the family during such a difficult time. That was exactly my goal, and I’m grateful to Presti’s for serving me. My criticism relates to the people who work at the counter. When I arrived, there were several people there, but I couldn’t find a queue. Since I had a specific time (13:00, but it was already 12:45 – I had informed them about the situation in advance), and I had already paid, I asked a staff member where I should go to pick up my order. I must say, I’ve been in better places before, considering we just got out of the Lakeview cemetery under extremely difficult circumstances—I was freezing, I cried a lot, and I was parked illegally. The woman who answered almost scolded me for not having a number, as if I were a child. It’s rare to encounter such disregard from a stranger, but I managed to get some response from her. Just by asking a question. Okay… so I got a number. And I waited. There were at least 4 people behind the counter, and a customer came in from time to time. Everyone ignored me until my number was called. When I spoke to the man at the counter, telling him that I had a prepaid order with my name on it, I felt he wasn’t very interested. I was told “we’re still working on it.” Okay… a few minutes passed, and the staff rushed around. At this point, I started to worry, as everyone who came from the cemetery had already been at the dinner for some time. Finally, a friendly young woman asked if I had been served, and I explained what I was waiting for. She said she would check the status, and a few minutes later, another woman brought a beautiful tray of cheesecakes and other sweets. I don’t know what happened, but the “I don’t care” attitude I felt when picking up my order was the last thing I expected from a famous institution in Cleveland. I’m very aware that we are rewarded for what we give, and I try to treat people kindly. Although I arrived with a broken heart, I didn’t deserve the lack of respect I received at first. So, probably I’ll think twice next time.

state: Milk Bar, located in the Cosmo, fittingly right next to momofuku, is a great spot to satisfy your sweet tooth! So many options - cookies, cake, crack pie, soft serve, cake pops, milkshakes. The best thing to get here is the soft serve hands down! You can split even the smaller size into 2 flavors and the best is the cereal milk and chocolate pretzel side by side. Add the corn flake crunch - they put it on the top/sides and there's a surprise layer on the bottom too! You will not be disappointed. Also delicious as an affogato and less sweet. Cookies are great to take on the go as they are packaged and you can also get a gift box to bring back as well. Unfortunately they also taste a bit like they are packaged too. Nonetheless, the best flavors are the corn cookie and compost cookie! The rest of the treats, like the crack pie or milkshakes, are good for a one time try or a taste but probably not as repeat orders since they are really super sweet.

state: Hey, I don’t want to criticize Amelie’s. There have been many nights when I really wanted a caramel salted brownie. They’re always available when you need them. In fact, Amelie’s never closes—it’s open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. If there’s anything they do well, it’s that. However, I must say that the quality has declined. When I go there now, I’m not surprised if I get an éclair that isn’t fresh or properly cooked. That’s part of “Amelie’s” charm. And, of course, there are all those “hipsters” too. You’ll have to find a place to sit, because those guys fill up all the seats. It can be a bit annoying when you just need a spot to park for 10 minutes. But no, you have to enjoy your desserts and coffee, and then move on. They have coffee, tea, sandwiches, soups, and lots of desserts. If you feel like eating around 6 p.m., wait 5 hours and then go to Amelie’s—less people to deal with, and therefore better desserts.

state: It's my first time trying the Jack Frost Donuts. The place is a little small but what you expect from donut stores? The lady there was so friendly. She helped us to pick the donuts cause we got overwhelmed by tons of different donuts and flavors! I tried my first sprinkle donut out of a box of dozen I got, and it tasted like heaven! For sure I will come back for more. Even the peanut butter frost was totally mesmerized me! If you're a peanut butter lover then you should totally get the donut with the pb frost. Speaking of frost, the frost they have on the donuts are amazing. They don't get messy in the box even though they get pressed by the top of the box unlike any other soft frost. It's totally worth two hours drive from Columbus. I love Jack Frost Donuts!!!

state: It’s obvious that my experience at the Milk Bar falls into the category of a “complex” experience. But really, I feel that a four-star rating is the final verdict. I’ve visited there several times. I keep coming back because the original “milk quake” was really good. I still miss it, so I come back in hope of not being disappointed repeatedly. I can happily say that in the last three visits (probably about six months ago, and in different places in the US), I didn’t encounter the poor consistency that came with a three-star rating. The ice cream isn’t exactly what I remember, but the consistency of “milk quake” has been… consistent—good, dense, and with chunks. I hated writing this sentence as much as you hated reading it. For what it’s worth, I asked someone at the East Village unit why I had such inconsistent experiences in the past. She said it was due to the heating of the ice cream balls, which caused the ice cream to melt. But that shouldn’t happen. So if it does, I should return it and ask them to fix it. Obviously, it’s not exactly that, but you get the idea. In short, and more precisely: if you love something, don’t give up on it. Maybe you should give up if it disappoints you constantly, but do some thorough research first. You might be satisfied with the result. My part is done.

However, the flavor of the ice cream seemed more like a Wendy’s smoothie with syrup than a real ice cream smoothie. But overall, it was pretty good. My recommendation: order a smoothie and then go for a walk by the water, or rent a raft.

state: Talk about paradise. As I walked into Sinful Sweets the displays of fudge led to the rows of truffles and my child-like wonder was in full force as I debated between dark chocolate graham crackers, chocolate smores, and a dark chocolate New York truffle. Needless to say, my wonderment led to me trying all three. The chocolate was so smooth and very rich. I love dark chocolate and the truffle stood out from the crowd. It was delicious. I also tried the chocolate covered bacon which was nothing short of miraculous. But sometimes the food isn't enough for a place to get a good review and Sinful Sweets offers plenty more. The staff working was great. It came up that I am visiting from Raleigh and we began talking about the differences in areas. He was very friendly, personable, and funny. My friends and I were able to sit on the benches in the front of the store and hang out while the shop was slow and talk with the staff. The final perk of Sinful Sweets is the price. They are dirt cheap, I felt. I absolutely intend on visiting this place again whenever I am in town.

state: There's a saying now that we eat with our eyes and this place is a prime example of picture perfect dessert. Not only the dessert is well put together, the interior as well. Now there's a big trend going on with grassy walls with neon signs and there's one implemented here to show off your dessert! These places are definitely a reminder that we're slowly started to get all the "Cali-like" boba/ ice cream places. Phoenix is really needing more places like this and I'm very happy it's in a prime spot. They're located next to Pokitrition, near off the 101 and Ray. The cool thing is that the creators of Pokitrition also made this place too! I didn't get to try the boba just yet but the ice cream is great. While being one of the reasons I don't have a 6 pack yet, this just makes it worse cause I'd probably be craving this place. KITH Treats is also a place that I get reminded of about this concept. This place is going to blow up and be packed. I'll be back for more. CERTIFIED BANGER
